limits: The fixed-order first pass is exploratory. Deployment, time, object placement and compilation history remain confounded.
Fresh object IDs do not prove fresh physical hardware or an empty platform compilation cache.
Module IDs and construction counters identify software instances, rather than physical hosts.
Conditioning uses a separate public-input Wasm module, rather than production private AES.
Equal logical auxiliary allocation does not equalize page residency, allocator state or compilation.
CPU includes complete participant invocations. Stage durations are wall time, with clock precision limits.
Conditioning cost includes A forwarding and B work. Front CPU is unmeasured; client conditioning elapsed includes its latency.
Client restoration includes inventory polling and request round trips.
The idle interval excludes client touches. Recovery alarms and platform eviction remain possible.
Phase names describe planned order. Actual gaps and instance identities govern warm/reuse interpretation.
These bounded replacement screens do not measure sustained signatures per minute or public SDK latency.
